newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daiwa Securities down over watchdog inspection.
newsitem.headline: Daiwa Securities down over watchdog inspection.

text.p: Daiwa Securities Co Ltd shares fell sharply in Thursday afternoon trade on anxieties sparked by what Daiwa said was a routine inspection by Japan's securities watchdog.
As of 0536 GMT, the shares were down 46 yen at 900.
"Dealers started loss-cutting sales after news spread that the SESC was conducting an inspection," a trader at a foreign brokerage said.
Brokers added that market sentiment was weak to begin with, and it was becoming a viscious circle, as falls in the share price were prompting more selling.
A Daiwa spokesman told Reuters that the securities watchdog had been conducting the inspection since March 3, and that the checks were routine and not related to suspicious deals.

"Rumours appear to be circulating that we might hold a news conference on the inspection, but we have no such plan now," he said. "But if the rumours are prompting rapid falls in the stock prices, then it is possible that we would give some explanation."
